To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) family physicians in Toronto have a high degree of consensus regarding which patients they discuss AIDS and its prevention and to whom they recommend HIV antibody testing for; 2) there is less consensus regarding whether they discuss AIDS with all sexually promiscuous patients; and 3) there is no consensus as to whether they should discuss AIDS with all patients.

90% or more of the family physicians surveyed discussed AIDS with patients in high risk groups, sexual partners, and those with many sexual contacts, and 90% or so recommended HIV antibody testing to patients in high risk categories who requested it.
